conventions.convention: Inputs are nonempty finite regular link diagrams. The empty diagram is excluded; a crossingless k-component diagram has bracket δ^(k−1), with δ=−A²−A^(−2).

In the positively oriented source chart, the overbranch runs southwest–northeast. A pairs left endpoints and right endpoints with weight A; B pairs top endpoints and bottom endpoints with weight A^(−1). Charts transport by orientation-preserving changes.

Crossing sign is sign det_P(v_over,v_under), where (u,v) is positive in P exactly when (n,u,v) is positive in ambient space. Positive and negative curls have factors −A³ and −A^(−3); normalization is (−A³)^(−wr(D)) times the raw bracket.
Braid time increases bottom to top, but positive projection coordinates are (t,x). A positive crossing is C_i=AI+A^(−1)e_i, with e_i the top-cap/bottom-cup pairing.
The trace dictionary uses q=A^(−2), t=A^(−4), z₀=−1/(t+1), and R_A=Z[A±1,(A^(−4)+1)^(−1)]. The unnormalized diagram trace assigns δ^k to k circles, whereas the bracket assigns δ^(k−1).
Ambient-link invariance of the normalized bracket assumes Countable Choice.
Comparison with the library Jones invariant assumes full Choice and uses t=A^(−4). Positive σ₁³ has Jones value t+t³−t⁴.
The state-sum algorithm accepts a typed mathematical diagram and specifies neither string parsing nor malformed-encoding rejection.

load_bearing.statement: For a nonempty unoriented regular link diagram D, the Kauffman bracket is the sum over S:C(D)→{A,B} of A^(a(S)−b(S))δ^(|S|−1), with δ=−A²−A^(−2) and the stated orientation-preserving smoothing convention.

For the declared n-strand operators, n≥2, C_i=AI+A^(−1)e_i and C_i⁻=A^(−1)I+Ae_i satisfy C_iC_i⁻=C_i⁻C_i=I and C_iC_(i+1)C_i=C_(i+1)C_iC_(i+1). Consequently every local Reidemeister II or III replacement preserves the bracket, with arbitrary strand orientations.

Adding a positive type-I kink multiplies the raw bracket by −A³ and increases writhe by 1; adding a negative kink multiplies it by −A^(−3) and decreases writhe by 1. Deletion uses reciprocal factors. Consequently f_D(A)=(−A³)^(−wr(D))⟨D⟩ is unchanged by every oriented Reidemeister move and planar isotopy.

For β∈B_n, n≥1, oriented in the braid direction, under v↦A^(−4) and z↦−1/(A^(−4)+1), ⟨β̂⟩=δ^(n−1)(−A)^e(β) tr_n(π_n(β)). The one-strand identity closure has bracket 1; positive and negative Markov stabilizations multiply the raw bracket by −A³ and −A^(−3).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If two nonempty regular oriented link diagrams represent ambient-isotopic oriented links, their writhe-normalized bracket values are equal. Thus f_D defines an invariant of nonempty oriented links.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every nonempty oriented link K, the normalized bracket is independent of its regular oriented diagram and satisfies V_K(t)=f_K(t^(−1/4)), where V_K is the stated library Hecke-trace Jones specialization.

For a typed nonempty unoriented regular link diagram D, the state-sum algorithm terminates after exactly 2^|C(D)| state visits and returns the displayed bracket sum. It makes no parsing or malformed-encoding claim.

seams_checked.note: The determinant order, induced projection orientation, positive Artin sign, and total writhe match the supplier. Local calculations do not use its separate normal-bundle framing assertion.
The conventions definition and BMW dictionary preserve the source-chart A/B pairings. Their separate Dubrovnik parameters and curl coefficients are not attributed to the bracket supplier.

The crossing relation and R2/R3 uses agree with the bracket convention. The framed S³ evaluator explicitly uses δ times the nonempty bracket and separately assigns 1 to the empty link; the annular expansion likewise defines its own empty-state value.

The ribbon comparison reproduces the exact Hecke specialization and accounts for the extra factor δ in categorical closure. Its Countable Choice hypothesis concerns trace-to-closure identification; it makes no unsupported Jones-invariance assertion.

The statewise Euler calculation uses the same A/B states and writhe. It explicitly sets q=−A^(−2), so q+q^(−1)=δ. The final Jones comparison retains full Choice and distinguishes reduced knot from unreduced link normalization.

The complexity results cite exactly 2^c state visits and the exact state sum. Their additional indexed bit-cost implementation is proved separately, excludes arbitrary parsing, and retains Countable Choice only for ambient-link invariance.

The smoothing operators match the positive-coordinate calculation. Crossing minimality uses normalized-bracket invariance under Countable Choice; Jones-span conversion uses the full-Choice comparison and t=A^(−4).
The coefficient definition preserves full Choice, x=t^(1/2), t=A^(−4), and the library normalization. The status remark does not use the bracket results to assert an unknot-detection theorem.
